## Direct Answer: What Is the Examination Scheme for SSC CHSL 2026? > [!IMPORTANT] > **Core Fact**: The Staff Selection Commission Combined Higher Secondary Level (**SSC CHSL 10+2**) examination is conducted in two mandatory stages: **Tier-1** (a 60-minute qualifying Computer Based Test consisting of 100 questions for 200 marks with 0.50 negative marking) and **Tier-2** (the merit-deciding stage conducted on a single day, comprising Session I with 120 objective questions across Mathematics, Reasoning, English, General Awareness, and a 15-question Computer Knowledge module for a total of 360 merit marks + 45 qualifying marks, followed immediately by Session II's mandatory Skill/Typing Test). Final appointment to prestigious Central Ministries is determined **100% on Tier-2 Section-I and Section-II scores**, provided candidates qualify both the Computer Knowledge module and the Typing Test. Every year, over 30 to 35 Lakh 12th-pass aspirants across all 28 Indian States and 8 Union Territories register for the SSC CHSL examination. Serving as the primary recruitment channel for Group 'C' ministerial positions across the Central Government of India, SSC CHSL offers stable desk careers with guaranteed 7th Central Pay Commission increments, Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS) benefits, residential government quarters, and structured promotional avenues to Gazetted officer grades. --- ## SSC CHSL Posts, Ministry Allocations & 7th CPC Pay Scale Under the 7th Central Pay Commission (7th CPC), SSC CHSL recruits for three distinct job profiles across vital Union Ministries (Home Affairs, External Affairs, Defence, Finance, Railways, Agriculture, and Electronics & IT), Constitutional Commissions (UPSC, Election Commission, CAG), and Central Appellate Tribunals: | Post Designation | Participating and Auditor General of India (CAG), Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change | **Level-5** | ₹29,200 – ₹92,300 | **₹51,000 – ₹56,500 / month** (Includes DA 53%+, HRA 30%, Transport Allowance) Classification for HRA (House Rent Allowance)**: > - **Class X Cities (30% HRA)**: Delhi/NCR, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Pune. > - **Class Y Cities (20% HRA)**: State capitals and major cities (e.g., Lucknow, Patna, Jaipur, Bhopal, Chandigarh, Kochi, Nagpur, Ranchi). > - **Class Z Cities (10% HRA)**: All other district headquarters, rural towns, and field postings. --- ## Multi-Stage Selection Architecture for SSC CHSL ```mermaid graph TD A[One-Time Registration OTR on ssc.gov.in] --> B[Tier-1 CBT: Screening Exam 100 Qs / 200 Marks / 60 Mins] B -->|Shortlisted Candidates ~10x Vacancies| C[Tier-2 CBT Session I: Written Merit 360 Marks + Computer 45 Marks] C --> D[Tier-2 Session II: Skill Test / Typing Test on Same Day] D --> E[Post-Preference Submission on Candidate Portal] E --> F[Document Verification DV by Allocating Ministry] F --> G[Final Merit Empanelment & Appointment] ``` 1. **One-Time Registration (OTR) & Application**: Candidates complete online registration on the official unified Staff Selection Commission portal (`https://ssc.gov.in`) with live webcam photographic capture and digital signature upload. 2. **Tier-1 Computer Based Screening Examination**: 100 multiple-choice questions for 200 marks in 60 minutes across 4 equal sections. Normalization is applied across multi-day shifts to shortlist candidates for Tier-2 in an approximate 1:10 ratio. 3. **Tier-2 Computer Based Merit Examination**: Conducted in a single multi-session sitting comprising: - **Section-I**: Mathematical Abilities (30 Qs) + Reasoning & General Intelligence (30 Qs) = 180 Marks. - **Section-II**: English Language & Comprehension (40 Qs) + General Awareness (20 Qs) = 180 Marks. - **Section-III Module-I**: Computer Knowledge Module (15 Qs × 3 = 45 Marks, Qualifying). 4. **Tier-2 Session II Typing / Skill Test**: Undertaken immediately on the same date following Session I. - **DEO**: Mandatory computer speed of 8,000 to 15,000 key depressions per hour. - **LDC / JSA**: Typing speed of 35 w.p.m. in English OR 30 w.p.m. in Hindi. 5. **Post-Preference Option Form**: Following the declaration of Tier-2 written results, qualified candidates submit their department and post preferences online. 6. **Departmental Document Verification (DV) & Medical Fitness**: The allocating ministry conducts document verification (matriculation certificate, 10+2 marksheet, caste/EWS certificates) and basic medical clearance. --- ## Tier-1 Examination Pattern & Section-Wise Weightage Tier-1 serves as a competitive preliminary screening test. While its marks do not contribute to the final merit ranking, candidates must secure high normalized scores to cross category-wise cutoffs. | Section / Subject Domain | Questions | Maximum Marks | Mark Weightage Graph | Sectional Focus Areas | |---|---|---|---|---| | **English Language (Basic Knowledge)** | 25 Questions | 50 Marks | [BAR:25%:English Language] | Spot the Error, Fill in the Blanks, Synonyms, Antonyms, Spellings, Idioms & Phrases, Cloze Passage | | **General Intelligence & Reasoning** | 25 Questions | 50 Marks | [BAR:25%:Reasoning] | Semantic Analogies, Symbolic/Number Operations, Figural Classification, Series, Syllogisms, Venn Diagrams | | **Quantitative Aptitude (Basic Arithmetic)** | 25 Questions | 50 Marks | [BAR:25%:Quantitative Aptitude] | Number Systems, Percentages, Ratio, Profit & Loss, Simple/Compound Interest, Algebra, Geometry, Mensuration | | **General Awareness (Static GK & Current)** | 25 Questions | 50 Marks | [BAR:25%:General Awareness] | History, Culture, Geography, Economic Scene, General Policy, Scientific Research, Current Affairs | | **Grand Total (Tier-1 Examination)** | **100 Questions** | **200 Marks** | **[BAR:100%:Total Composite]** | **Composite Time: 60 Minutes (80 mins for PwD scribe)** | > [!CAUTION] > **Negative Marking in Tier-1**: Exactly **0.50 marks (25% penalty)** are deducted for every incorrect option chosen. Since questions carry 2 marks each, uncalculated guessing severely damages your normalized score and can easily drop your rank below the cutoff line! --- ## Tier-2 Comprehensive Merit Examination Pattern (The Final Merit Stage) Tier-2 determines your All India Rank (AIR), post preference allocation, and ministry cadre. It is divided into **two sessions conducted on the same day**: ### Session I (Written Merit & Computer Module — Total Duration: 2 Hours 15 Minutes) | Section | Module & Subject | Questions & Marking | Maximum Marks | Allotted Time | Evaluation & Merit Rules | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | **Section I** | **Module-I**: Mathematical Abilities
**Module-II**: Reasoning & General Intelligence | 30 Questions × 3 Marks

**Module-II**: General Awareness | 40 Questions × 3 Marks

Negative marking: **-1 mark**. | | **Section III** | **Module-I**: Computer Knowledge Module | 15 Questions × 3 Marks | **45 Marks** | **15 Minutes** (20 mins for scribe) | **Strictly Qualifying** in nature (Minimum qualifying marks: UR 30% [13.5 marks], OBC/EWS 25% [11.25 marks], SC/ST 20% [9 marks]). Failure in Computer eliminates your entire candidature! | | **Sub-Total** | **Merit Deciding Score (Section I + Section II)** | **120 Questions** | **360 Marks** | **2 Hours 15 Mins** | **Final Cutoff is computed out of 360 Marks!** | ### Session II (Skill Test & Typing Test Module — Conducted on the Same Day) | Part | Applicable Post | Test Type | Speed / Key Depression Requirement | Test Duration | Permissible Error Threshold | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | **Part A** | **Data Entry Operator (DEO) in CAG & Ministries** | Speed Data Entry | **15,000 Key Depressions per hour** (~3,750 key depressions in 15 mins) | **15 Minutes** | UR: 5% maximum permissible error; Reserved: 7% error | | **Part B** | **Data Entry Operator (DEO Grade 'A') in other Offices** | Speed Data Entry | **8,000 Key Depressions per hour** (~2,000 key depressions in 15 mins) | **15 Minutes** | UR: 5% maximum permissible error; Reserved: 7% error | | **Part C** | **Lower Division Clerk (LDC) / Junior Secretariat Assistant (JSA)** | Typing Test (Passage Typing) | **English: 35 words per minute** (~10,500 KDPH / 1,750 keys in 10 mins)
OR
**Hindi: 30 words per minute** (~9,000 KDPH / 1,500 keys in 10 mins) | **10 Minutes** | UR: **7% maximum permissible error**; OBC/EWS/SC/ST: **10% maximum error** | > [!IMPORTANT] > **Typing Test Medium Selection**: Candidates select their typing medium (English or Hindi) while filling out the online application form. English typing is conducted on standard QWERTY keyboards; Hindi typing offers choice between **Inscript keyboard** and **Remington (CBI) keyboard** layouts. If no choice is selected, English is applied by default. --- ## Granular Topic-Wise Syllabus Breakdown for SSC CHSL ### 1. Mathematical Abilities (Tier-1: 25 Qs / 50 Marks | Tier-2: 30 Qs / 90 Marks) #### A. Number Systems & Basic Arithmetic Operations - **Computation of Whole Numbers, Decimals & Fractions**: VBODMAS priority, recurring decimals, terminating vs non-terminating decimals, surds and indices simplifications. - **Relationships Between Numbers**: Divisibility tests (2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 11, 13), prime factorization, Highest Common Factor (HCF) and Least Common Multiple (LCM) application word problems. - **Percentages, Ratio & Proportion**: Successive percentage changes, expenditure-consumption formulas, direct and inverse proportions, third/fourth proportionals, mean proportional. - **Square Roots & Cube Roots**: Long division method, shortcut estimation, rationalizing the denominator. - **Averages & Mixtures**: Weighted average, age-based equations, replacement in groups, rule of alligation for price and concentration problems. - **Interest**: Simple Interest ($SI = \frac{PRT}{100}$), Compound Interest calculated annually, half-yearly, and quarterly; difference between CI and SI ($D_2 = P(r/100)^2$). - **Profit, Loss & Discount**: Cost Price, Selling Price, Marked Price, successive discounts, false weights and dishonest merchant problems. #### B. Algebra & Advanced Mathematics - **Basic Algebraic Identities**: $(a \pm b)^2$, $(a \pm b)^3$, $a^3 \pm b^3$, $a^3+b^3+c^3-3abc = (a+b+c)(a^2+b^2+c^2-ab-bc-ca)$ and its conditional cases when $a+b+c=0$. - **Linear Equations**: Solving equations with one and two variables, graphs of linear equations, conditions for consistency (unique, infinite, no solution). - **Geometry (Elementary Concepts)**: Properties of triangles (incenter, circumcenter, orthocenter, centroid), similarity and congruence of triangles, circles (tangents, intersecting chords, alternate segment theorem), common transverse and direct tangents. - **Mensuration (2D & 3D)**: Areas and perimeters of triangles, quadrilaterals, regular polygons, circles. Surface areas and volumes of right circular cylinders, cones, spheres, hemispheres, rectangular parallelepiped, and right pyramids with triangular/square bases. - **Trigonometry**: Trigonometric ratios ($\sin, \cos, \tan, \cot, \sec, \csc$), fundamental identities ($\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$, $1+\tan^2\theta=\sec^2\theta$, $1+\cot^2\theta=\csc^2\theta$), standard angles ($0^\circ, 30^\circ, 45^\circ, 60^\circ, 90^\circ$), heights and distances (elevation and depression angles). - **Statistical Charts & Data Interpretation**: Histogram, Frequency polygon, Bar-diagram, Pie-chart, Measures of Central Tendency (Mean, Median, Mode) for grouped and ungrouped datasets. --- ### 2. General Intelligence & Reasoning (Tier-1: 25 Qs / 50 Marks | Tier-2: 30 Qs / 90 Marks) - **Semantic & Figural Analogies**: Letter shifting, word association, mathematical logic, symbolic operations. - **Symbolic & Number Classification**: Odd-one-out among numbers, alphabet clusters, dictionary ordering. - **Semantic, Number & Figural Series**: Number progression patterns, double series, matrix series, missing number grids. - **Coding and Decoding**: Shift cipher, reverse alphabet values ($A=26, Z=1$), substitute symbol coding, conditional coding rules. - **Blood Relations**: Family tree diagrams, coded relationships ($P+Q$ means $P$ is mother of $Q$), pointing-to-photograph puzzles. - **Venn Diagrams & Syllogisms**: 2-set and 3-set overlapping representations; Syllogistic deductions involving *all*, *some*, *no*, and modern *only a few* / *at least* premises. - **Direction Sense Test**: 8-point compass navigation, shadow orientation at sunrise and sunset, Pythagoras distance theorems. - **Seating Arrangements & Order-Ranking**: Single linear rows facing North/South, double parallel rows, circular arrangements (facing center/outside), vertical ranking by marks/height. - **Non-Verbal Reasoning**: Mirror and water images, paper folding and punched hole patterns, embedded hidden figures, completion of incomplete geometric figures, counting figures (triangles, squares, straight lines). - **Critical & Analytical Reasoning (Tier-2 Exclusive)**: Statement and Assumptions, Statement and Conclusions, Cause and Effect, Statement and Arguments, Course of Action. --- ### 3. English Language & Comprehension (Tier-1: 25 Qs / 50 Marks | Tier-2: 40 Qs / 120 Marks) > [!TIP] > **The 120-Mark Deciding Weightage in Tier-2**: In Tier-2 Section-II, English represents **40 questions out of 60 (66.7% of Section II marks)**. Achieving 35+ correct responses in English is practically mandatory to compete for top ministry allocations (MEA, CSS, AFHQ). - **Grammar & Sentence Structure**: Subject-Verb Agreement, Tenses (Simple, Continuous, Perfect, Perfect Continuous), Conditional Clauses (Zero, First, Second, Third Conditionals), Prepositions, Conjunctions, Articles, Noun and Pronoun cases. - **Error Spotting & Sentence Improvement**: Identifying grammatical, structural, or diction errors across divided sentence segments; replacing underlined phrases for syntax refinement. - **Active and Passive Voice**: Transformation of assertions, interrogatives, imperatives, and modal auxiliary sentences across all active tenses. - **Direct and Indirect Speech (Narration)**: Conversion of statements, questions, exclamations, and requests with appropriate tense shifts, pronoun changes, and time-adverb adjustments. - **Vocabulary Building**: Synonyms and Antonyms, Homonyms, One-Word Substitutions, Idioms and Phrases, Spelling mistakes / detecting misspelled words. - **Reading Comprehension & Cloze Test**: 5-to-10 question Cloze passages testing contextual vocabulary and grammatical flow; narrative, discursive, and analytical reading comprehension passages testing central idea, tone, vocabulary in context, and direct factual inference. - **Para Jumbles (Sentence Rearrangement)**: Reconstructing coherent 4-sentence paragraphs ($P, Q, R, S$) by identifying opening introductory sentences, pronoun linkages, transition markers, and logical conclusions. --- ### 4. General Awareness (Tier-1: 25 Qs / 50 Marks | Tier-2: 20 Qs / 60 Marks) - **Indian History**: Indus Valley Civilization, Vedic Period, Buddhism & Jainism, Maurya & Gupta Dynasties, Delhi Sultanate, Mughal Administration, 1857 Uprising, Socio-Religious Reform Movements, Freedom Movement (1885–1947), Important Governor-Generals and Viceroys. - **Art & Culture**: Classical dance forms (Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Sattriya, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam) and associated Sangeet Natak Akademi maestros, regional folk dances, music gharanas, traditional festivals, UNESCO World Heritage Monuments in India. - **Indian & World Geography**: Physiographic divisions of India (Himalayas, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Coastal Plains, Islands), major river systems and tributaries, multipurpose dams, climate and monsoon cycles, soil classification, national parks and biosphere reserves, solar system, atmosphere layers. - **Indian Polity & Constitution**: Historical evolution, Preamble, Fundamental Rights (Articles 12–35), Directive Principles of State Policy (Articles 36–51), Fundamental Duties (Article 51A), President, Vice-President, Prime Minister & Council of Ministers, Parliament (Lok Sabha & Rajya Sabha), Supreme Court & High Courts, Constitutional Amendments, Emergency Provisions. - **Indian Economy**: National Income metrics (GDP, GNP, NNP), Inflation indices (CPI, WPI), Fiscal Policy, Union Budget, Taxation (Direct & Indirect / GST), Monetary Policy of Reserve Bank of India (Repo, Reverse Repo, CRR, SLR), Five-Year Plans, Banking structure. - **General Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)**: 10th NCERT foundation; Newton's laws of motion, units and measurement, human anatomy and organ systems, vitamins and deficiency disorders, chemical names and formulas (baking soda, bleaching powder, Plaster of Paris), acids, bases and salts. - **Current Affairs (National & International)**: Major government flagship schemes, appointments (Chief Justice, Cabinet Ministers, Army Chief, International Body heads), sports championships (Olympic & Paralympic Games, Cricket World Cups, Asian Games, Grand Slams), bilateral military exercises, prestigious national awards (Bharat Ratna, Padma Awards, Khel Ratna, Sahitya Akademi). --- ### 5. Computer Knowledge Module (Tier-2 Section-III: 15 Questions / 45 Marks) Although qualifying in nature, scoring below the cutoff threshold (UR: 30% / 13.5 marks) results in instantaneous disqualification regardless of a perfect 360/360 in Sections I and II! - **Computer Basics**: Organization of a computer system, Central Processing Unit (CPU), input/output devices, computer memory (RAM, ROM, Cache, Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD), memory organization, back-up devices, ports, Windows Explorer, keyboard shortcuts. - **Software & Operating Systems**: Basics of system software, operating systems (Windows, Linux, macOS), application software, device drivers. - **Working with Internet and Emails**: Web browsing and search engines, downloading and uploading files, managing email accounts, e-banking portals, basics of cloud storage. - **MS Office Essentials**: - **MS Word**: Document creation, paragraph alignment, margins, page breaks, header and footer, table formatting, spell check, mail merge. - **MS Excel**: Spreadsheets, cell formatting, formulas ($SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, IF, VLOOKUP$), charts and graphs, freezing panes. - **MS PowerPoint**: Slide templates, transitions, animations, slide master view. - **Basics of Networking and Cyber Security**: Network types (LAN, WAN, MAN), networking devices (modem, router, switch, gateway), network topology (bus, star, ring, mesh), internet protocols ($TCP/IP, HTTP, HTTPS, FTP$), cyber threats (viruses, worms, trojans, ransomware, phishing, spyware), firewalls, antivirus mechanisms. --- ## Recent Cut-Off Trends for SSC CHSL (Tier-1 General Candidate Benchmark) | Recruitment Cycle | Unreserved (UR) | Other Backward Classes (OBC) | Economically Weaker Section (EWS) | Scheduled Caste (SC) | Scheduled Tribe (ST) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | **SSC CHSL 2024 (Tier-1)** | **157.72** | **156.80** | **151.10** | **139.30** | **130.65** | | **SSC CHSL 2023 (Tier-1)** | **153.91** | **152.26** | **151.02** | **136.41** | **124.52** | | **SSC CHSL 2022 (Tier-1)** | **157.72** | **153.25** | **151.02** | **135.46** | **125.79** | | **SSC CHSL 2021 (Tier-1)** | **140.18** | **140.12** | **131.40** | **112.86** | **104.78** | > [!NOTE] > **Target Score Benchmark**: Due to fierce competition among over 30 Lakh candidates, aim for a raw score of **160+ out of 200 in Tier-1** and **310+ out of 360 in Tier-2** to secure your top choice of ministry located in Delhi/NCR. --- ## 100% Free Preparation Resources & Official PDF Links > [!RESOURCE] > You do not need expensive coaching programs to crack the SSC CHSL examination! The following verified, official government portals and free open-source materials cover 100% of the syllabus: | Resource Title | Material Type & Description | Direct Access Link | |---|---|---| | **Official SSC Unified Portal** | Application, OTR, Notifications & Candidate Corner | [Visit Official SSC Portal](https://ssc.gov.in) | | **Official SSC CHSL Notification & Syllabus PDF** | Complete Official Scheme of Examination | [Download Official Notification PDF](https://ssc.gov.in) | | **Free NCERT Class 6–10 Textbooks** | Foundation Science, History, Geography & Polity Books | [Download Free NCERT Books](https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php) | | **Free Swayam Online Mathematics & English** | Government-sponsored Video Lectures & Concept Notes | [Access Swayam Portal](https://swayam.gov.in) | | **Free Keyboard Typing Practice Engine** | DEST & Typing Test Speed Simulator | [Practice Free Typing Drills](https://www.typing.com/student/tests) | | **Sarkari Aavedan Age Relaxation Calculator** | Calculate exact age against SSC cutoff dates | [Use Free Age Calculator](/tools/age-calculator) | | **Sarkari Aavedan Photo & Signature Resizer** | Resize images to exact SSC specifications (20–50 KB) | [Use Free Image Resizer](/tools/image-resizer) | | **Sarkari Aavedan Live Vacancy Alerts** | Browse active SSC and Central Government Job openings | [View Live Government Jobs](/latest-jobs) | --- ## High-Impact 90-Day Step-by-Step Preparation Protocol ### Phase 1: Conceptual Foundation & Topic Coverage (Days 1 to 35) - **Daily Mathematics (2.5 Hours)**: Master fundamental arithmetic (Percentages, Ratio, Time & Work, Profit & Loss). Make handwritten formula cheat sheets for geometry and algebra identities. - **Daily English (2 Hours)**: Read one editorial from standard national dailies daily. Memorize 20 new idioms, one-word substitutions, and phrasal verbs every evening. - **Daily Reasoning (1.5 Hours)**: Practice 40 questions of syllogisms, coding-decoding, number series, and non-verbal rotation patterns. - **Daily General Awareness (1.5 Hours)**: Read NCERT Polity (Constitution & Preamble) and Modern Indian History. Maintain monthly current affairs summaries. - **Typing Practice (30 Minutes)**: Practice touch typing on a physical keyboard using all 10 fingers. Target 25 w.p.m. with 95% accuracy by Day 35. ### Phase 2: Previous Year Questions (PYQs) & Speed Drills (Days 36 to 70) - **Solve 3,000+ PYQs**: Complete chapter-wise previous year question compilations from 2020 through 2025 examinations. - **Computer Knowledge Preparation**: Spend 45 minutes daily studying computer basics, MS Office shortcuts, and networking protocols. - **Typing Speed Acceleration**: Push typing speed to **38–42 w.p.m.** on random 10-minute newspaper passages. ### Phase 3: Full-Length Mocks & Exam Simulation (Days 71 to 90) - **Daily Timed Mock**: Attempt one full 100-question Tier-1 mock every morning in the exact 60-minute window (e.g., 9:00 AM – 10:00 AM). - **In-Depth Error Journaling**: Spend 2 hours analyzing errors. Categorize mistakes into *Calculation Error*, *Lack of Knowledge*, or *Time Pressure Misread*. - **Tapering & Mental Rest**: Stop taking new mock tests 48 hours before your exam day. Focus exclusively on formula sheets, vocabulary flashcards, and positive mental visualization. --- ## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) ### Q1: Is SSC CHSL Tier-1 qualifying or are its marks added to the final merit list? **Ans**: SSC CHSL Tier-1 is **strictly qualifying in nature**. The marks obtained in Tier-1 are used solely to shortlist candidates for the Tier-2 examination. The final merit list and department allocations are decided **100% on the basis of marks scored in Tier-2 Section-I and Section-II (Total 360 Marks)**, subject to qualifying the Computer Knowledge module and the Skill/Typing test. ### Q2: What is the negative marking penalty in SSC CHSL Tier-1 and Tier-2? **Ans**: In **Tier-1**, each wrong answer incurs a deduction of **0.50 marks** (questions carry 2 marks each). In **Tier-2**, each incorrect response in Section-I, Section-II, and Section-III Module-I results in a penalty of **1 mark (-1 mark deduction)** (questions carry 3 marks each). There is no negative marking for unattempted questions. ### Q3: What is the minimum typing speed required for LDC, JSA, and DEO posts in SSC CHSL? **Ans**: For **Lower Division Clerk (LDC)** and **Junior Secretariat Assistant (JSA)**, candidates must achieve a typing speed of **35 words per minute (w.p.m.) in English** (equivalent to 10,500 key depressions per hour) OR **30 words per minute (w.p.m.) in Hindi** (equivalent to 9,000 key depressions per hour) in a 10-minute test. For **Data Entry Operator (DEO Grade A)**, candidates must achieve **8,000 key depressions per hour** (approx 2,000 key depressions in 15 minutes); for **DEO in the Office of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)**, the required speed is **15,000 key depressions per hour** (approx 3,750 key depressions in 15 minutes). ### Q4: Can a candidate who passed 12th Standard from Arts or Commerce apply for DEO in CAG? **Ans**: No. For the post of Data Entry Operator (DEO Grade 'A') in the Office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG), Ministry of Environment, and select technical ministries, candidates must have passed **12th Standard in Science stream with Mathematics as a compulsory subject**. However, 12th-pass candidates from **any stream (Arts, Commerce, Science, Humanities)** are fully eligible for Lower Division Clerk (LDC), Junior Secretariat Assistant (JSA), and general DEO posts in all other Union Ministries. ### Q5: What happens if a candidate scores high in Tier-2 written sections but fails the Computer Knowledge Module? **Ans**: If a candidate fails to achieve the minimum qualifying cutoff in the Computer Knowledge module (UR: 30% [13.5/45 marks], OBC/EWS: 25% [11.25/45 marks], SC/ST: 20% [9/45 marks]), they are **completely disqualified from the recruitment process**, regardless of whether they achieved a top or even perfect score in the Section-I and Section-II written merit tests. Therefore, candidates must allocate serious preparation time to the Computer Knowledge module.
